source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: You have dozens of skills installed, yet a conversation that uses none of them is no more crowded than before. What explains that, per the lecture?

options.text: Each skill is compressed into a much shorter summary before it is stored
options.feedback: Compression is not the mechanism. The instruction body is not shrunk at all -- it is simply left out of context until a request needs it.

options.text: The harness unloads and deletes any skill that has not been used for a while
options.feedback: Deleting unused skills was not part of the explanation given, and it would mean losing a skill rather than simply not paying its context cost yet.

options.text: Only a skill's name and description stay in context; the rest loads when it triggers
options.feedback: An idle skill costs almost nothing, because only its short name and description are resident. The body, the scripts, and the reference files enter context only once a request actually matches it.

options.text: Every skill is capped at the same fixed token length no matter what it does
options.feedback: A cap would not distinguish an idle skill from an active one. The point was about when a skill's content loads, not how long any one skill is allowed to be.
